about: The film of the website. The numbers (the length of the film, the start and end of each chapter, the lines) are written by tools/prepare-film.py from the data file the film is made with; do not change them by hand. The rest is the site's own: a chapter begins with the shot fromShot and runs to the next chapter; stillAfter is the moment of its still, in seconds from its start.

film.name: I wish I could build it
film.description: A short film about Teamwright. Somebody wants to build a small sensor hub, a board, its firmware and a case, and runs the project as the manager of a team of AI specialists. The interface in the film is the real program on a sample project; the board, the parts and the case are modelled for the film.

chapters.title: The wish
chapters.seen: A desk at night under one lamp. A notebook holds a pencil sketch of a small box with a screen. A board, firmware and a case are too much for one person. Then the laptop opens on Teamwright.

still.alt: The first screen of Teamwright after it is installed: no project yet, and a button to start one.

chapters.title: Tell the Advisor
chapters.seen: The real program. The brief is typed, the Advisor asks its questions, then proposes three specialists and a plan of fourteen tasks. The manager approves.

still.alt: The proposal of the Advisor: the project in its words, a team of three specialists with a model and an effort for each, and a plan of fourteen tasks with their owners and what each waits for.

chapters.title: One plan, every view
chapters.seen: The same project four days into its first sprint: the board of the sprint, the backlog with its sprints, story points and burndown, the list, the Gantt chart, the calendar and the dashboard. Then the chooser that adds a view, and the office with two specialists at work.

still.alt: The Backlog view: the sprint that runs, with its dates, its story points and its burndown, the planned sprint, and the backlog under them.

chapters.title: The team at work
chapters.seen: From a lamp of the office into a workshop: three benches, a lamp over each, one for each specialist.

still.alt: The office while a specialist works: a plan of a workshop with a bench for every member of the team, and the lamp over the working one lit.

chapters.title: Schematic becomes board
chapters.seen: On the bench of the hardware engineer a schematic draws itself in gold, and its lines sink into a bare board. Then the view glides low over the finished board: its pads, its tracks, its vias and its print.

still.alt: A specialist at work on a task: the panel of the task shows every step it takes as it happens.

chapters.title: A choice waits for you
chapters.seen: The parts land on the board. The task that is the manager's, ordering the boards and parts, waits for the manager.

still.alt: The inbox of the manager: a question from a specialist, with the options, what each leads to, and the one it recommends.

chapters.title: The case comes down
chapters.seen: On the bench of the mechanical designer the case closes round the board.

still.alt: The board of a sample project cut into three areas, Electronics, Firmware and Enclosure: its tasks in five statuses from To do to Done.

chapters.title: It lives
chapters.seen: The closed device lands on the desk. A hand pushes a USB-C plug in, and the screen comes on with its readings: carbon dioxide, temperature and humidity. The person at the desk looks at it and is glad.

still.alt: A specialist has finished a task: the steps it took, its report, and the model, the tokens and the time the work took.

chapters.title: Teamwright
chapters.seen: The mark of Teamwright, and where to find it.

still.alt: The mark of Teamwright: a letter T laid out of five blocks, the one that holds the others in gold.

lines.text: I want to build a sensor hub.
A board. Firmware. A case.
I wish I could.
Teamwright exists.
Tell the Advisor what you want.
It asks what it needs to know.
Then it proposes a team and a plan.
You approve it.
Now your plan is a board.
Four days into the first sprint.
Run it in sprints, with a backlog, story points and a burndown.
See the same plan as a list, a Gantt chart, or a calendar.
The dashboard says where the project stands.
Add the views you need.
Specialists do the work, each on its task.
Schematic. Layout.
When a choice is yours, it waits for you.
Board, firmware, enclosure. One plan.
You decide. You build it.
You manage. Your team does the work.
This is just the beginning.
Changing how projects are managed, and what one developer can build.
Open source. Runs on your own Claude Code.
